{"subject":"Cassandra leaderboard p99 and GC pauses","body":"Hi Lior,

Thanks for connecting. Your talk on running 60 self-managed Apache Cassandra nodes for the Kestrel Games leaderboard cluster stood out, especially the tail latency and GC/compaction tuning side.

One thing relevant to that workload: ScyllaDB uses a shard-per-core C++ architecture with no JVM garbage-collection pauses, which is aimed at keeping p99 latency predictable. It speaks CQL, so it can be evaluated against an existing Cassandra data model.

If it's useful, I'm happy to share how others have approached leaderboard-style workloads with it.

Oz
GTM Engineer, ScyllaDB

Reply STOP to opt out.","evidence_ids":["s06"],"value_prop_ids":["vp_latency"],"context_fact_ids":[]}
